qa.text: The white_pot mesh lines up well with the real pot's rim, body and handle, but its base is missing, so about a fifth of the pot's interior floor is uncovered in the frame. The mesh also has a slit in its left wall, a lumpy surface and a plain rod handle with the hanging hole filled in, and it misses the left marker ball.

The projected mesh covers most of the lid. It leaves a notch at 1 o'clock and an uncovered crescent of rim from there to 4 o'clock, which matches a missing wedge and a bent flap in the mesh rim. The mesh also has a through-hole in the plate under the handle, markers that are only shallow bumps instead of balls on stems, and a lumpy surface with a ragged rim.

The pot's outer outline and pose match well. Only a 6-8 px strip on the left edge of the handle tip is uncovered. The mesh itself is defective: the floor is mostly missing, there is a hole in the left inner wall near the rim, the surface is lumpy, a stray thin flap sits inside the bowl, and the handle's hanging hole is filled in.

The fit is good. The mesh tint covers the spoon and its markers, apart from a thin uncovered sliver about 2-3 px wide along the left and lower-left edge of the bowl. In the side view of the 3-D mesh the neck where the handle meets the bowl is pinched noticeably thinner than the handle, which is a minor shape quirk this top-down frame cannot verify.

The pose is good: the rim, bowl and handle outlines match the real pot. The submitted white_pot mesh (library_v3) is defective. It has a large hole through the bowl bottom, about 7-8 cm wide, and a second hole about 5 cm tall in the side wall, crossed by a thin broken-off strip of rim. Its surface is rough and its wall thickness is uneven. The holes are why the inner floor and the inner left wall show untinted in the overlay.

The submitted wooden_spoon mesh fits the real spoon well in frame 240: bowl, neck, handle and markers all line up, with at most a few pixels of offset at the handle end. The 3-D mesh matches the description: a thin oval shallow bowl, a long straight round handle and the marker balls, with no visible missing parts, blobs or holes.

The tracked pose fits the white pot well. The mesh has a large hole through the floor and a smaller one in the inner left wall, so those parts of the real pot are not covered when the mesh is projected. The mesh surface is also ragged: the rim outline is uneven, a thin stray sliver sits inside the bowl, and the red overlay edge is lumpy where the hand grips the handle.

The wooden_spoon mesh is placed well. The red tint traces the real bowl and handle closely, with at most a 1 px edge offset. The mesh itself looks right: an oval bowl about 30% of the total length, a long straight round handle, and three marker balls in the right places. I see no clear shape defect, though the 3-D views do not show whether the bowl is hollowed.

From this camera view the projected mesh matches the real tumbler within a few pixels, so the tracked pose looks right. The mesh itself is broken: it is two separate closed pieces, a rounded lump at the wide end with no rim or opening and a strip tilted about 25-30 degrees for the narrow half, with a large gap between them, a rough and blotchy surface, and no marker balls that can be identified.

The tracked pose fits well; the outline matches the real white pot all the way around, including the handle. The submitted mesh, though, is missing most of the pot's floor and has a hole in the upper-left inner wall, so those areas are left uncovered in the projection, and its walls are rough with a stray thin flap inside the bowl.

The projected blue_cup mesh is slightly off toward the lower right: it misses the upper-left rim and the left marker, and spills about 10 px onto the holding hand. A small untinted dark spot inside the silhouette matches the mesh hole. The mesh itself has a large hole through the wall near the wide end, a torn and ragged wide-end edge, a lumpy, dented wall, and a cross-section that is not round at mid-height and the cap.

The beige_cup mesh is poor: two separate, flattened, voxel-blocky pieces with fins, no round rim or opening, and an uneven side profile. Its projection still covers the cup in the right place at the right size, but it misses a band along the near rim, a thin strip inside the left rim and both marker balls, and small bits of tint stick out past the right rim.

The pose fits well, but the mesh is poor. It leaves a wedge of the real rim uncovered at the upper-left and has a small see-through gap inside the opening. The mesh also has a large ragged hole in its wall near the wide end, a lumpy wall surface, blocky stair-stepped facets, a loose strip at one edge, and too little taper in the side view.

The pose fits well, but the submitted dish-rack mesh is missing most of its tray floor, so the real white tray shows through between the pegs in the projection. The surface is also lumpy, with ribbed artifacts on the cup holder.

The pose and outer outline match well, but the mesh is missing most of the tray floor, so about 20% of the real object (the white floor between the pegs) is left uncovered. The pegs are only short stubs or blobs, with the back row fused to the wall, and the surface is lumpy.

The submitted wooden_spoon mesh (library_v3) fits the real spoon well in eval 15, frame 0. The bowl, the handle and the three marker balls all sit where they are in the photo, with no visible shift or rotation. The renders show the right shape: a shallow oval bowl, a long straight handle with a slight bend at the neck, and proportions close to the real spoon. I found no shape defects.

The tracked pose and outer outline fit well. The mesh is missing most of the tray floor, so much of the real tray interior shows through as holes. The fins are rebuilt as fused, rounded knobs, and the surface is rippled, especially on the cup holder.

The submitted wooden_spoon mesh (an oval shallow bowl, a long straight handle and marker balls) looks right in shape and proportion. With our tracked pose it lands on the real spoon to within a few pixels. The only part that can't be checked is the handle end, which is hidden under a blurred hand.

The projected mesh matches the mini_sweeper closely in this frame, with only small gaps at the bristle tips and the lower body corner. The mesh itself is lumpy and noisy, its ring handle is uneven with an off-centre hole and a small spur, and the marker balls are low bumps rather than balls on stems.

The pose fits closely, but the projected mesh leaves a thin strip (about 3 px) of the upper-left wall rim uncovered and puts the ring hole too far right, so the tint spills over the fingertips. The mesh itself has stair-step terracing across the scoop face, a lumpy, ragged surface, an irregular egg-shaped ring hole and no visible marker-ball bumps.

The projected mesh covers the cup well, except for a thin crescent of uncovered wall (about 7-13 px) on the left of the rim. The mesh has a hole and a large missing section of wall at the wide end, a lumpy surface, and almost no taper in its side view, so its cross-section is not round. The rim miss most likely comes from these mesh defects at the wide end, since the rest of the outline lines up.

The eval-20 water_pitcher mesh is positioned and oriented correctly, but it has holes through the bowl wall: the side render shows one, and the overlay is missing tint over the real inner wall, with the largest gap about 45x10 px. It also has a small lump of about 5-8 px on the upper spout edge, and the handle sits about 5 px too far right, with mesh filling part of the gap between the handle and the body.

The tracked pose lines up with the board well. The faults are all in the mesh: a large spurious hole (with an island inside) near one end, which leaves untinted patches in the projection; the missing side slot; a diagonal crease and uneven, lumpy thickness; and markers modelled only as fused bumps, with the top marker left uncovered.

The pose fit is good. The mesh is missing the slot that runs from one long edge to about mid-width, its rim is slightly lumpy, and the tops of the two top-corner marker balls stick out past the projected mesh.

The pose is right and the outer outline fits, apart from a small bulge past the right end. The mesh is missing most of the tray floor, though, so the real floor between the fins is uncovered. Its fins are short lumpy blobs, and in the renders one row looks disconnected rather than being thin, flat fins standing on a floor.

The white_pot pose is right: the projected outline matches the bowl and the full handle. The problem is the mesh, which has a large hole in the bowl floor and a smaller torn hole in the upper-left inside wall with a loose strip at its edge, plus a noisy, lumpy surface.

The projected mesh covers the visible wooden handle, but it stops about 5-7 px short of the visible bristle tips and tilts slightly down-left; the hand hides most of the body. The mesh itself has a small round through-hole in the body, a loose tab sticking into the ring opening, and a mildly irregular, non-oval ring outline.

The submitted dish-rack mesh is missing most of its tray floor between the fin rows, apart from a patch at the far end. That leaves the real floor uncovered over about two-thirds of the tray and along the inner front wall, while the outer outline fits well, about 8 px long at the far end. The thin floor ridges at the far end are also not modelled.

The projected silhouette mostly fits, but a red skirt flares past the cup's base onto the thumb and table, and a thin strip of the real upper-left wall is left uncovered. The mesh itself has a large jagged hole in the wall toward the open end, a ragged open rim with loose flaps, dented walls, an oval cross-section in the middle and toward the open end, and a squarish stepped patch on the flat end instead of a round base.

The submitted wooden_spoon mesh (library_v3) has the right shape: an oval, thin, shallow bowl, a long straight handle and the marker balls, in proportions that match the photo. The tracked pose places it accurately on the spoon resting on the table, with only a tiny under-coverage at the left side of the neck.

The tracked pose fits the cup well. The visible gaps come from the mesh: the wall has a large hole and is torn away at the wide rim (so the strip inside the mouth is uncovered), and two marker balls are missing. The mesh is also lumpy, and its cross-section is not round: one side view tapers and the other is nearly straight.
In eval 33, frame 24, the submitted wooden_spoon mesh fits the real spoon well with no visible pose error. No mesh-shape problem is visible either.

The projected mesh fits the spoon well. The only flaw is a small uncovered sliver where the bowl meets the handle. That sliver comes from the mesh shape: its bowl is an ellipse with an abrupt neck, while the real spoon narrows gradually into the handle.

The wooden_spoon mesh fits the eval-36 frame well: no rotation or length error. The only shortfall is a 2-4 px (a few millimetres) uncovered strip along the far edge, widest where the bowl narrows into the handle. The bowl in the render also shows cosmetic lengthwise faceting.

The eval-37 wooden_spoon mesh fits the frame well: the bowl, handle and markers line up within about 1 px. The one flaw is that the mesh's bowl-to-handle join is a little narrower and more abrupt than the real spoon's gradual taper, which leaves thin slivers of real wood (about 2-3 px above, 1-2 px below) uncovered at the neck.

The pose is right and the mesh covers the dust pan closely. The small misses all come from the mesh: its ring hole is pinched and irregular, so the tint covers part of the real hole, and the grey lip's bottom tip and two mocap balls under the edge are left uncovered. The mesh surface itself has stair-step terracing on the scoop and lumpy, ragged outer edges.
